name: vol_adjusted_reversion_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Standard mean-reversion strategies use fixed z-score thresholds (e.g., 2.0 sigma), but the optimal threshold varies with the current volatility regime. In low-vol environments, a 1.5-sigma deviation is significant and likely to revert. In high-vol, even 2.5-sigma deviations may be noise. By dynamically scaling the entry z-score threshold based on the ratio of current 30-min realized vol to 120-min realized vol, we adapt the mean-reversion strategy to the local volatility environment. When vol is compressing (30min_vol < 120min_vol), use tighter thresholds (1.5 sigma); when vol is expanding, require wider thresholds (2.5+ sigma). This captures more mean-reversion trades in calm periods and avoids false signals in volatile periods.
mechanism: Short-term selling exhausts available demand at a price level, creating a temporary liquidity vacuum. Market makers who absorbed the selling begin marking prices back to reduce inventory risk. Limit buy orders resting below create a floor, and new participants entering the long side accelerate the reversion as the forced selling pressure dissipates.

indicators.name: adaptive_threshold
indicators.formula: 1.5 + 1.0 * vol_ratio  # ranges from ~1.5 (low vol) to ~3.0 (high vol)

conditions: close < vwap (below VWAP, institutional buy territory)

exit.signal_exit: if vol_ratio > 2.0 (vol regime shift during trade), exit

weaknesses: The adaptive_threshold formula (1.5 + 1.0 * vol_ratio) is ad-hoc and not derived from first principles; optimal coefficients may differ by stock and regime
In rapidly changing vol environments (vol_ratio crossing 1.0 back and forth), the threshold flickers, generating whipsaw entry signals
Higher trade frequency (3-6/day) means transaction costs compound; the per-trade edge must be consistently positive, which is hard with 1-min noise
prior_art: Bali & Cakici (2004) volatility and cross-section returns; adapted for intraday with dynamic thresholds. Similar to Kaufman (2013) adaptive moving average concept applied to mean-reversion thresholds.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
